sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: A little more than a year ago, in February of 2021, it was snowing in Austin, Texas, which is unusual.
sentences.zh: 大约一年多前，也就是2021年2月，德克萨斯州奥斯汀下雪了，这很不寻常。

sentences.en: So this is the beginning of what might be a historic winter storm here in Austin.
sentences.zh: 所以，这可能是一场历史性冬季风暴在奥斯汀的开端。

sentences.en: I love this.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个。

sentences.en: I mean, I was psyched.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我当时兴奋极了。

sentences.en: It was snowing, like really snowing in Austin, and that just, it doesn't happen much here.
sentences.zh: 下雪了，奥斯汀真的下雪了，这儿平时可不怎么下雪。

sentences.en: Moe's Bouchelle is a reporter at KUT, the local public radio station in Austin, Texas.
sentences.zh: 莫·布歇尔是德克萨斯州奥斯汀当地公共广播电台KUT的一名记者。

sentences.en: So, you know, I just wanted to get out and document this storm as much as I could.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我只是想出去尽可能多地记录这场风暴。

sentences.en: But then there's this moment in the tape that, I mean, it still gives me chills when I listen back to it.
sentences.zh: 但录音里有那么一刻，我是说，现在回听时依然让我不寒而栗。

sentences.en: Big question for a lot of people right now is whether the electric grid is going to hold up.
sentences.zh: 现在很多人最大的疑问是电网能否撑得住。

sentences.en: If you remember the news from Texas, the grid did not hold up.
sentences.zh: 如果你还记得当时德州的新闻，电网没撑住。

sentences.en: It went down pretty much all over the state.
sentences.zh: 几乎全州都停电了。

sentences.en: In fact, millions lost power for days, some in houses not built to withstand freezing temperatures.
sentences.zh: 事实上，数百万人断电了好几天，有些人住的房子根本无法抵御冰冻气温。

sentences.en: According to at least one estimate, more than 800 people died.
sentences.zh: 据至少一项估算，有超过800人死亡。

sentences.en: I am so f***ing heated, y'all.
sentences.zh: 我真是气炸了，各位。

sentences.en: Greg Abbott, what the f*** are you going to do about this power grid?
sentences.zh: 格雷格·阿博特，你到底打算怎么处理这个电网问题？

sentences.en: See all these headlights?
sentences.zh: 看到这些车灯了吗？

sentences.en: You see all these people?
sentences.zh: 看到这些人了吗？

sentences.en: These are people that have had no electricity for 13 hours, and they don't have anywhere else to go.
sentences.zh: 这些人已经断电13个小时了，他们无处可去。

sentences.en: Day five, and nothing.
sentences.zh: 第五天了，还是什么都没有。

sentences.en: Moe's has been covering energy in Texas for more than a decade.
sentences.zh: 莫报道德州能源问题已经超过十年了。

sentences.en: He reported on the whole blackout catastrophe with his colleagues at KUT,
sentences.zh: 他和KUT的同事们报道了整场停电灾难，

sentences.en: and they made a great podcast out of that reporting called The Disconnect.
sentences.zh: 他们还根据这些报道制作了一档很棒的播客，叫《断连》。

sentences.en: And today on our show, we wanted to talk with Moe's about what exactly happened a year ago
sentences.zh: 今天在我们的节目中，我们想和莫聊聊一年前到底发生了什么，

sentences.en: and how it connects to the strange history of the Texas power grid.
sentences.zh: 以及它与德州电网那段奇特的历史有何关联。

sentences.en: So a few days after the blackout ended, you know, we started talking about making a podcast
sentences.zh: 停电结束后几天，我们开始商量做一期播客，

sentences.en: just to explain what happened because people really didn't understand.
sentences.zh: 就是为了解释发生了什么，因为人们真的没搞明白。

sentences.en: I was hearing all these questions about the Texas power grid, how it works,
sentences.zh: 我当时听到各种关于德州电网的问题，它是如何运作的，

sentences.en: and how something so catastrophic could happen in a state that is literally known for its energy industry, right?
sentences.zh: 以及在一个以能源产业闻名的州，怎么会发生如此灾难性的事件，对吧？

sentences.en: It's baked into the entire persona of the state.
sentences.zh: 这已经融入了这个州的整体形象中。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, I know Texas is huge when it comes to oil production,
sentences.zh: 我知道德州在石油生产方面规模巨大，

sentences.en: but can you give us a sense of just how big oil production is?
sentences.zh: 但你能让我们感受一下石油产量到底有多大吗？

sentences.en: Okay, so to give you like a sense of scale, about 15% of the entire world's oil is produced in the United States,
sentences.zh: 好的，为了让你有个概念，全世界约15%的石油产自美国，

sentences.en: and almost half of that is produced right here in Texas.
sentences.zh: 而其中近一半就产自德州。

sentences.en: That's a lot.
sentences.zh: 那确实很多。

sentences.en: Yeah, but it's not just oil.
sentences.zh: 是的，但不仅仅是石油。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of people don't know this, but Texas is also the number one producer of wind in the country.
sentences.zh: 很多人不知道，德州也是全国最大的风能生产地。

sentences.en: We're number one in gas, too, not to mention solar, nuclear, coal.
sentences.zh: 我们的天然气产量也是第一，更不用说太阳能、核能和煤炭了。

sentences.en: All of that makes what I'm about to say next really surprising.
sentences.zh: 所有这些使得我接下来要说的话显得格外令人惊讶。

sentences.en: The Texas energy grid for decades has operated kind of on this knife's edge.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，德州能源电网一直处于一种如履薄冰的状态。

sentences.en: I mean, in the few months after the last blackout, there were two more times Texans were warned
sentences.zh: 我是说，在上一次停电后的几个月里，德州人又两次收到警告，

sentences.en: that there might not be enough electricity to go around.
sentences.zh: 称电力可能供应不足。

sentences.en: Two.
sentences.zh: 两次。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So if you had to sum it up, why?
sentences.zh: 所以如果让你总结一下，为什么？

sentences.en: Why is the Texas grid so fragile?
sentences.zh: 为什么德州电网如此脆弱？

sentences.en: Why is it on this knife's edge?
sentences.zh: 为什么它总是如履薄冰？

sentences.en: That's a big question.
sentences.zh: 这是个大问题。

sentences.en: To answer it, we've really got to look back at the whole history of the grid
sentences.zh: 要回答这个问题，我们真的得回顾一下电网的整个历史，

sentences.en: and how Texas came to be what we call an energy island.
sentences.zh: 以及德州是如何成为我们所说的“能源孤岛”的。

sentences.en: It's the only state in the lower 48 that operates its own independent electric grid.
sentences.zh: 它是美国本土48州中唯一运营自己独立电网的州。

sentences.en: Okay, so let's get to that history.
sentences.zh: 好的，那我们来聊聊那段历史。

sentences.en: So we're going to start at the very beginning, right?
sentences.zh: 我们从最开始说起，好吗？

sentences.en: Right when electricity comes out.
sentences.zh: 就在电力刚出现的时候。

sentences.en: And at first, it's kind of a novelty, right?
sentences.zh: 起初，这算是个新鲜事物，对吧？

sentences.en: But then people, you know, they start having in their houses, cities especially,
sentences.zh: 但后来人们，你知道，开始在家里使用它，城市尤其如此，

sentences.en: they start using it to power streetlights, maybe streetcars.
sentences.zh: 他们开始用它来驱动路灯，或许还有电车。

sentences.en: And as electricity expands, there was kind of this, like, hodgepodge mix of ways you could get it, of utilities.
sentences.zh: 随着电力普及，出现了一种大杂烩式的获取方式，也就是公用事业公司。

sentences.en: There were some utilities that were run by cities and towns.
sentences.zh: 有些公用事业由城市和城镇运营。

sentences.en: And then there were, like, these independent outfits, private operators.
sentences.zh: 还有一些是独立的机构，私人运营商。

sentences.en: Like, at the beginning, like, literally a person could kind of, like, buy a kit.
sentences.zh: 就像刚开始时，一个人甚至可以买套设备，

sentences.en: You know, you get an electric generator and you set up shop and you just start trying to compete for customers.
sentences.zh: 你知道，弄台发电机，开门营业，然后就开始竞争客户了。

sentences.en: So it's kind of like the Wild WeSt.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像“狂野西部”。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was very unregulated.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常缺乏监管。

sentences.en: But all of that starts to change as it becomes more of a necessity.
sentences.zh: 但随着它变得越来越不可或缺，这一切开始改变。

sentences.en: Starting in 1907, states began to regulate power companies.
sentences.zh: 从1907年开始，各州开始监管电力公司。

sentences.en: This is Julie Cohn.
sentences.zh: 这是朱莉·科恩。

sentences.en: She wrote a book about the history of power in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 她写过一本关于美国电力历史的书。

sentences.en: It's called The Grid.
sentences.zh: 书名叫《电网》。

sentences.en: They said, you know, this is becoming an essential service.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这正在成为一项基本服务。

sentences.en: We want to make sure that it's provided on a fair basis to the citizens of our state.
sentences.zh: 我们想确保它能公平地提供给本州公民。

sentences.en: So we will say who can operate where and how much you can charge your customers for your electric service.
sentences.zh: 所以我们将规定谁可以在哪里运营，以及你向客户收取多少电费。

sentences.en: And you, in return, will promise us that you will be fair in how you provide electricity to your customers and it will be reliable.
sentences.zh: 作为回报，你向我们承诺，你提供电力的方式会是公平的，而且是可靠的。

sentences.en: So this regulation she's talking about, it was happening in most states, like the state was regulating the utilities, but not in Texas.
sentences.zh: 所以她提到的这种监管，在大多数州都在进行，即州政府监管公用事业，但在德州却不是这样。

sentences.en: I can't say I'm surprised.
sentences.zh: 我一点也不惊讶。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, Texas was anti-regulation even back then.
sentences.zh: 我是说，德州即使在当时也是反监管的。

sentences.en: So the oversight of our power companies here remained pretty light.
sentences.zh: 所以我们这里的电力公司监管一直很宽松。

sentences.en: But as the grid grew elsewhere in the country, and especially as it started crossing state lines, regulation became a bigger issue.
sentences.zh: 但随着电网在全国其他地方扩张，特别是当它开始跨越州界时，监管就成了一个更大的问题。

sentences.en: Because then it becomes a national issue because then it becomes the purview of the federal government if it goes across the state.
sentences.zh: 因为一旦跨州，它就成了国家层面的问题，也就归联邦政府管辖了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yes, it does.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And it really changed in a big way when when this guy became president.
sentences.zh: 当这个人成为总统时，情况发生了巨大的变化。

sentences.en: Let me assert my firm belief that the only thing we have to fear is fear itself.
sentences.zh: 让我坚定地重申我的信念：我们唯一需要恐惧的，就是恐惧本身。

sentences.en: This guy is FDR, of course.
sentences.zh: 这个人当然就是富兰克林·罗斯福（FDR）。

sentences.en: This nation is asking for action and action now.
sentences.zh: 这个国家要求行动，而且是立即行动。

sentences.en: So this was the New Deal era, OK, and FDR was going after monopoly power all over the place.
sentences.zh: 那是“新政”时期，罗斯福正在到处打击垄断势力。

sentences.en: And these big electric companies, they were among his main targets.
sentences.zh: 而这些大型电力公司就是他的主要目标之一。

sentences.en: They had become increasingly monopolistic as all these discreet local grids grew into each other and became more of these bigger kind of regional entities.
sentences.zh: 随着所有这些分散的本地电网相互连接，并演变成更大的区域性实体，它们变得越来越垄断。

sentences.en: And FDR wanted to check that power, especially, you know, to make sure that rate payers didn't get a raw deal.
sentences.zh: 罗斯福想要遏制这种权力，特别是为了确保纳税人不会受到不公平对待。

sentences.en: So Congress passed a law in 1935 that said if you crossed state lines, well, you're going to be under the regulation of the feds.
sentences.zh: 因此，国会在1935年通过了一项法律，规定如果你跨越州界，那么你就要接受联邦监管。

sentences.en: And the key phrase there that I'm hearing is cross state lines.
sentences.zh: 我听到的关键短语是“跨越州界”。

sentences.en: It sounds like you can get around federal regulation if these companies didn't cross state lines.
sentences.zh: 听起来如果这些公司不跨越州界，就能绕过联邦监管。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that is what happened in Texas.
sentences.zh: 而这正是德州发生的情况。

sentences.en: You know, you can imagine why it was very attractive to these Texas power companies to say, OK, forget it.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象为什么这对德州电力公司很有吸引力，他们会说，好吧，算了吧。

sentences.en: We're not going to sell power to anybody in Louisiana or Oklahoma or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我们不向路易斯安那州、俄克拉荷马州或其他任何地方卖电。

sentences.en: We're just going to form interconnected systems inside Texas and operate as we wish.
sentences.zh: 我们就在德州内部形成互联系统，随心所欲地运营。

sentences.en: I think it's interesting to note that at first, Texas was not alone in this.
sentences.zh: 我认为值得注意的是，起初德州并非孤例。

sentences.en: Some other utilities stayed within state lines, too.
sentences.zh: 其他一些公用事业公司也留在了州界内。

sentences.en: Maine had no interconnections, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，缅因州就没有互联。

sentences.en: But by the 1960s, Texas was the only state left in the contiguous United States with its own grid.
sentences.zh: 但到了20世纪60年代，德州成了美国本土唯一拥有独立电网的州。

sentences.en: And part of the reason why has to do with Texas's size.
sentences.zh: 而部分原因与德州的面积有关。

sentences.en: Texas, as everyone who lives in Texas knows, is a really big state.
sentences.zh: 正如每个住在德州的人都知道的那样，德州是一个非常大的州。

sentences.en: And not only are we big, but we're wide.
sentences.zh: 而且我们不仅大，还很宽。

sentences.en: We have two time zones.
sentences.zh: 我们有两个时区。

sentences.en: So the sun rises an hour later in West Texas than it does in East Texas.
sentences.zh: 所以西德州的日出比东德州晚一个小时。

sentences.en: So Texas is like width.
sentences.zh: 所以德州在宽度上很有特点。

sentences.en: It means that not everybody needs energy at the same time.
sentences.zh: 这意味着并不是每个人都需要在同一时间用电。

sentences.en: People in East Texas wake up, drink their coffee, turn on their air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 东德州的人起床、喝咖啡、打开空调。

sentences.en: And then gradually, an hour later, people in West Texas do the same thing.
sentences.zh: 然后过了一个小时，西德州的人才做同样的事情。

sentences.en: That is amazing to me that the reason why this holds together is that just the geography of the state.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到非常神奇，这个系统能维持下去的原因竟然仅仅是因为该州的地理位置。

sentences.en: So energy demand moves slowly across the state because it's so wide.
sentences.zh: 所以能源需求在州内缓慢移动，因为它太宽了。

sentences.en: And that means that the grid doesn't get overloaded.
sentences.zh: 这意味着电网不会超负荷。

sentences.en: No one's turning on their coffee machine all at once across an entire gigantic state.
sentences.zh: 不会整个巨大的州里所有人都同时打开咖啡机。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We can roll that power around.
sentences.zh: 我们可以调度电力。

sentences.en: And there's also the weather to think about.
sentences.zh: 而且还要考虑天气因素。

sentences.en: Electricity, you know, is needed more when there's extreme weather.
sentences.zh: 你知道，极端天气下对电力的需求更大。

sentences.en: But Texas is so big that there's really hardly ever a moment when there's the same weather all across the state.
sentences.zh: 但德州太大了，几乎从来不会出现全州天气完全相同的情况。

sentences.en: So that really lets you kind of move the power around to where it's needed.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实让你能够把电力输送到需要的地方。

sentences.en: And that's really important because having enough power to meet electric demand, that's critical.
sentences.zh: 这非常重要，因为拥有足够的电力来满足电力需求是至关重要的。

sentences.en: That is the name of the game.
sentences.zh: 这就是关键所在。

sentences.en: Otherwise, the entire system trips up and you start seeing blackouts.
sentences.zh: 否则，整个系统就会跳闸，你就会看到停电。

sentences.en: Maybe now we should talk about what is actually happening when a blackout happens.
sentences.zh: 也许现在我们应该谈谈停电时到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: What is actually happening when a grid trips up and fails?
sentences.zh: 当电网跳闸并失效时，到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: Okay, so this is fun.
sentences.zh: 好的，这很有趣。

sentences.en: I think the best way to explain this is to take you into a blackout.
sentences.zh: 我认为解释这一点的最好方法是带你进入一次停电现场。

sentences.en: So I'm going to take a break from Texas history now, and we're going to jump ahead in time to 1965.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我要暂停一下德州历史，我们要跳到1965年。

sentences.en: In 1965, the Northeast suffered one of the biggest power failures in U.S.
sentences.zh: 1965年，美国东北部遭遇了历史上最大的电力故障之一。

sentences.en: history.
sentences.zh: 历史。

sentences.en: And I'm going to play you the sound from that blackout.
sentences.zh: 我要给你播放那次停电时的声音。

sentences.en: That doesn't sound like a blackout.
sentences.zh: 那听起来不像停电。

sentences.en: That sounds like a song.
sentences.zh: 听起来像首歌。

sentences.en: So why are you playing a song?
sentences.zh: 那你为什么要放一首歌？

sentences.en: This is Everyone's Gone to the Moon by a guy named Jonathan King.
sentences.zh: 这是乔纳森·金演唱的《每个人都去了月球》。

sentences.en: And this was a big hit in 1965.
sentences.zh: 这是1965年的一首热门歌曲。

sentences.en: So on November 9th of that year, this song was playing on a radio station in New York City, WABC, when this blackout hit.
sentences.zh: 那年11月9日，当这次停电发生时，纽约市的WABC电台正在播放这首歌。

sentences.en: And what we're listening to is the tape of that broadcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我们听到的就是那次广播的录音。

sentences.en: So you can hear the music start to, like, wobble around a bit at the end there, sort of like its speed is changing.
sentences.zh: 你可以听到音乐在最后开始有点晃动，就像它的速度在改变一样。

sentences.en: And that's because of actually what's happening on the electric grid.
sentences.zh: 那是因为电网上实际发生的事情。

sentences.en: And a lot of people don't know this, but the grid has a beat.
sentences.zh: 很多人不知道，电网是有节拍的。

sentences.en: It's 60 hertz or 60 cycles per second.
sentences.zh: 它是60赫兹，也就是每秒60个周期。

sentences.en: And this is the frequency that electricity runs over transmission lines.
sentences.zh: 这就是电力在输电线上运行的频率。

sentences.en: Almost everything electrical in your house is built to run on this 60 hertz, your toaster, your TV.
sentences.zh: 你家里几乎所有的电器都是为了在这个60赫兹下运行而制造的，你的烤面包机、你的电视。

sentences.en: And at this radio station in New York, the turntables were synced to that frequency.
sentences.zh: 在纽约的这家电台，唱机是与该频率同步的。

sentences.en: So when the beat starts to slow down on the grid, the DJ starts to notice it in the music.
sentences.zh: 所以当电网上的节拍开始变慢时，DJ就开始在音乐中察觉到了。

sentences.en: Lazy river and the key of R.
sentences.zh: 懒河与R调。

sentences.en: Everything's running at half speed.
sentences.zh: 一切都在以半速运行。

sentences.zh: 第一是让该州许多地方的消费者能够选择自己的电力供应商，这就是我们之前谈到的。

sentences.en: But the second thing, and this is one of the most critical parts of all this, is that this bill created what's called an energy-only market.
sentences.zh: 但第二点，也是所有这些中最关键的部分之一，就是这项法案创造了所谓的“仅能源市场”。

sentences.en: So tell me more about that.
sentences.zh: 那跟我多讲讲这个吧。

sentences.en: What is an energy-only market?
sentences.zh: 什么是“仅能源市场”？

sentences.en: So Texas's energy-only market is the first and only one of its kind in the country.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯的“仅能源市场”是全国同类市场中的首个，也是唯一一个。

sentences.en: In most other parts of the country, a power plant is kind of paid just to sit around to provide energy just in case it's needed.
sentences.zh: 在全国其他大部分地区，发电厂即便只是闲置待命，以备不时之需，也能获得报酬。

sentences.en: But in Texas, power plants are only paid for the power that they produce and sell on the market.
sentences.zh: 但在德克萨斯，发电厂只有在市场上生产并售出电力时才能获得报酬。

sentences.en: People in favor of this system, they said it was the most efficient way to do things.
sentences.zh: 支持这种制度的人说，这是最高效的运作方式。

sentences.en: But critics looked at it and they said, wait a second, power plants can charge more for electricity the less of it there is available.
sentences.zh: 但批评者审视后却说，等一下，电力越稀缺，发电厂就能把电价定得越高。

sentences.en: You know, just like we were talking about with Enron, it kind of creates this incentive for scarcity.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像我们之前谈到安然公司时说的那样，这在某种程度上创造了一种对稀缺性的激励。

sentences.en: Okay, so I'm starting to see how this all fits together.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我开始明白这一切是怎么联系在一起的了。

sentences.en: Texas operates on its own grid to avoid federal regulation, making it the only energy island in the country.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州为了规避联邦监管，在自己的电网上运行，使其成为全国唯一的“能源孤岛”。

sentences.en: It's also been deregulated to the point where there's purposely almost no excess energy on the grid,
sentences.zh: 它还被去监管化到了一种程度，即刻意让电网上几乎没有多余的能源储备，

sentences.en: which means that when there's a huge surge in demand, like, say, I don't know, during a serious winter storm, a blackout isn't just likely.
sentences.zh: 这意味着当需求激增时，比如，我不知道，在一场严重的冬季风暴期间，停电不仅是可能的，

sentences.en: It's like, you know, almost a certainty.
sentences.zh: 简直可以说是几乎必然会发生的。

sentences.en: Yeah, and because it's an energy island, when the state's grid does go down, like, the cavalry isn't coming.
sentences.zh: 没错，而且因为它是一个能源孤岛，当州电网崩溃时，根本没有援军会来。

sentences.en: You're not going to be able to get energy from neighboring states the way that you can in the rest of the country.
sentences.zh: 你无法像全国其他地方那样从邻近州获取电力。

sentences.en: So this is where we found ourselves last year as this historic winter storm bears down on the state.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是去年那场历史性冬季风暴席卷该州时，我们所处的境地。

sentences.en: Demand for power is expected to potentially exceed supply during parts of Monday and Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 预计在周一和周二的部分时段，电力需求可能会超过供应。

sentences.en: Help us to keep the system from being overloaded.
sentences.zh: 请帮助我们防止系统过载。

sentences.en: Lower that thermostat just a little bit.
sentences.zh: 把恒温器调低一点。

sentences.en: So this unprecedented storm is coming.
sentences.zh: 所以这场前所未有的风暴即将来临。

sentences.en: How does the state begin to prepare?
sentences.zh: 该州开始如何准备？

sentences.en: So this is where ERCOT, the Reliability Council that we talked about earlier, comes back into the picture.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们之前提到的可靠性委员会——ERCOT（德克萨斯电力可靠性委员会）再次登场的时候了。

sentences.en: You remember ERCOT, you know, its job is to make sure that the grid doesn't break down, that we don't get to that point.
sentences.zh: 你还记得ERCOT吧，它的职责是确保电网不会崩溃，确保我们不会走到那一步。

sentences.en: And how does ERCOT do that now that it's in this completely deregulated energy market in Texas?
sentences.zh: 既然现在处于德克萨斯这种完全去监管化的能源市场中，ERCOT又是如何做到这一点的呢？

sentences.en: Okay, so they're still doing the traffic cop thing, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以他们还在扮演交通警察的角色，对吧？

sentences.en: They're trying to direct enough energy onto the grid to meet demand.
sentences.zh: 他们试图引导足够的能源进入电网以满足需求。

sentences.en: But like you said, now they're operating in this energy-only market, which means that the incentive, basically,
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，现在他们是在这种“仅能源市场”中运作，这意味着基本上，

sentences.en: for power generators is to operate as close to a blackout as possible, right?
sentences.zh: 对于发电商来说，激励机制就是让他们尽可能在接近停电的边缘运作，对吧？

sentences.en: You could even say that ERCOT is trying to manage a grid that's kind of working directly against their interests.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可以说，ERCOT试图管理的电网，其运作方式与他们的利益背道而驰。

sentences.en: It's like being an air traffic controller where the planes want to fly into the ground.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一个空中交通管制员，而飞机却想往地上撞一样。

sentences.en: I never thought of that before, but yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我以前从没想过这一点，但确实，确实如此。

sentences.en: So it's a lot of pressure to do the job.
sentences.zh: 所以这份工作压力很大。

sentences.en: There's a ton of pressure.
sentences.zh: 压力非常大。

sentences.en: And you can hear them feeling that pressure the afternoon before the storm started.
sentences.zh: 在风暴开始的前一天下午，你可以感受到他们承受着这种压力。

sentences.en: ERCOT is requesting all Texans to conserve energy today, Sunday, through Tuesday, February 16th, to the extent that they can do so safely and reliably.
sentences.zh: ERCOT请求所有德克萨斯人在今天（周日）到2月16日周二期间，在安全可靠的前提下尽可能节约用电。

sentences.en: This is ERCOT's VP of System Operations, Dan Woodfin.
sentences.zh: 这是ERCOT系统运营副总裁丹·伍德芬（Dan Woodfin）。

sentences.en: Here he's in a conference call with media.
sentences.zh: 他正在这里与媒体进行电话会议。

sentences.en: Basically, he's saying, hey, people, we should stop using electricity so that maybe a blackout doesn't happen.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是在说，嘿，各位，我们应该停止用电，这样或许就不会发生停电了。

sentences.en: But then the winter storm hits and people, reasonably enough, they just can't conserve electricity.
sentences.zh: 但随后冬季风暴来袭，人们出于合理的原因，根本无法节约用电。

sentences.en: They need it to heat their homes.
sentences.zh: 他们需要电力来为房屋供暖。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: People are cold.
sentences.zh: 人们感到寒冷。

sentences.en: I mean, during the storm, the airport in Dallas reported a 72-year low.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，风暴期间，达拉斯机场记录到了72年来的最低温。

sentences.en: It was negative two degrees in Dallas.
sentences.zh: 达拉斯的气温降到了零下二度。

sentences.en: So people are under distress and they need heat in their homes.
sentences.zh: 所以人们处于困境中，他们需要家中有暖气。

sentences.en: And so they cannot regulate their power the way that ERCOT wants them to.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们无法按照ERCOT的要求去调节用电。

sentences.en: But it seems to me that the other way to solve this is to have the power plants produce more power.
sentences.zh: 但在我看来，解决这个问题的另一种方法是让发电厂生产更多的电力。

sentences.en: Yeah, for sure.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: And ERCOT starts trying to do that.
sentences.zh: ERCOT也开始尝试这样做。

sentences.en: They start calling up power plants and saying, hey, if you can turn on, now is the time to do it.
sentences.zh: 他们开始致电发电厂说，嘿，如果你们能启动，现在就是时候了。

sentences.en: But a lot of power plants just can't come back online.
sentences.zh: 但许多发电厂根本无法重新上线。

sentences.en: This is the former CEO of ERCOT, Bill Magnus, talking about it back in February 2021.
sentences.zh: 这是ERCOT前首席执行官比尔·马格努斯（Bill Magnus）在2021年2月谈论此事时的录音。

sentences.en: One generator after another reported that they were tripped off.
sentences.zh: 一个接一个的发电机组报告说它们跳闸停机了。

sentences.en: They were not able to operate.
sentences.zh: 它们无法继续运行。

sentences.en: So for the power plants, the problem is that things just start to freeze up.
sentences.zh: 所以对于发电厂来说，问题在于一切都开始结冰了。

sentences.en: They're built in Texas for warm weather and they're built outside.
sentences.zh: 它们在德克萨斯是为了温暖天气而建造的，而且是露天建造的。

sentences.en: So their equipment is not winterized.
sentences.zh: 所以它们的设备没有经过防寒处理。

sentences.en: And suddenly in this super cold weather, they really literally cannot produce power.
sentences.zh: 突然在这样极寒的天气下，它们真的无法发电了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So like every part of this system is failing.
sentences.zh: 所以这个系统的每个部分似乎都在失效。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So ERCOT can't get any more power right when demand is surging.
sentences.zh: 所以就在需求激增时，ERCOT却无法获得更多电力。

sentences.en: And that means one thing.
sentences.zh: 这意味着一件事。

sentences.en: They've got to start cutting power across the state.
sentences.zh: 他们必须开始在全州范围内切断电力。

sentences.en: So that's what they do.
sentences.zh: 所以他们就是这么做的。

sentences.en: And with people's power getting cut, demand does start to drop.
sentences.zh: 随着人们的电力被切断，需求确实开始下降。

sentences.en: But that doesn't work because it turns out that as the demand is dropping because of these power cuts,
sentences.zh: 但这并没有奏效，因为事实证明，当需求因为这些断电而下降时，

sentences.en: the supply on the grid is still dropping faster than the demand.
sentences.zh: 电网上的供应下降速度比需求还要快。

sentences.en: Power plants are still breaking down all over the place.
sentences.zh: 发电厂仍在各地不断发生故障。

sentences.en: And at that point, we're getting down to the frequency levels where we're in the danger zone.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，我们正处于频率水平的危险区域。

sentences.en: Remember that beat of the grid that we talked about, how the system is built to run at that 60 hertz frequency?
sentences.zh: 还记得我们谈到的电网“心跳”吗？系统是按60赫兹的频率运行的。

sentences.en: You see, if the grid falls below 60 hertz for too long, it causes catastrophic grid failure.
sentences.zh: 你看，如果电网频率低于60赫兹太久，就会导致灾难性的电网崩溃。

sentences.en: That's not a planned blackout.
sentences.zh: 那不是计划内的停电。

sentences.en: It is a total breakdown.
sentences.zh: 那是彻底的瘫痪。

sentences.en: That would mean hospitals don't have electricity.
sentences.zh: 这意味着医院没有电。

sentences.en: Gas stations don't have electricity.
sentences.zh: 加油站没有电。

sentences.en: The government itself doesn't have electricity at the offices that they're using to try to manage this type of crisis.
sentences.zh: 政府本身在试图管理这种危机的办公室里也没有电。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I mean, that's just apocalyptic.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直是世界末日。

sentences.en: That's like Mad Max.
sentences.zh: 就像《疯狂的麦克斯》一样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's a humanitarian crisis.
sentences.zh: 这是一场人道主义危机。

sentences.en: It's maybe like nothing that we've ever seen before in this country.
sentences.zh: 这可能是我们在这个国家从未见过的景象。

sentences.en: So how does it end up unfolding for the people managing the grid that first night?
sentences.zh: 那么对于第一晚管理电网的人来说，最终结果如何呢？

sentences.en: So that first night, the frequency on the grid drops to 59.4 hertz, which is a key number because at 59.4, the clock starts.
sentences.zh: 第一天晚上，电网频率降到了59.4赫兹，这是一个关键数字，因为到了59.4，倒计时就开始了。

sentences.en: If you stay at 59.4 for nine minutes or more, generation units begin to trip off on their own.
sentences.zh: 如果你在59.4赫兹停留9分钟或更久，发电机组就会开始自动跳闸。

sentences.en: So the operators at ERCOT literally have nine minutes to get this thing right?
sentences.zh: 所以ERCOT的操作员真的只有9分钟来纠正这一切？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The way the grid is set up is that after nine minutes, power plants start disconnecting themselves across the state.
sentences.zh: 电网的设置方式是，9分钟后，全州的发电厂就会开始自动断开连接。

sentences.en: Like, imagine fighter pilots ejecting themselves from the plane before it crashes.
sentences.zh: 就像想象一下战斗机飞行员在飞机坠毁前弹射逃生一样。

sentences.en: That's effectively what power plants are doing, trying to save themselves from frying along with the rest of the grid.
sentences.zh: 这实际上就是发电厂在做的事情，试图保护自己免受与电网其他部分一起烧毁的命运。

sentences.en: So these operators at ERCOT, they have nine minutes to get things right or all those awful things we mentioned start happening.
sentences.zh: 所以ERCOT的这些操作员有9分钟的时间来纠正问题，否则我们提到的所有可怕的事情都会开始发生。

sentences.en: And, you know, what's worse for ERCOT is that as time ticks off, the number continues to drop.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，对ERCOT来说更糟糕的是，随着时间流逝，频率数字还在持续下降。

sentences.en: So they basically decide that they have to throw the kitchen sink at this thing.
sentences.zh: 所以他们基本上决定必须孤注一掷。

sentences.en: So they order this one massive final power cut to the grid.
sentences.zh: 于是他们下令对电网进行了最后一次大规模的切断。

sentences.en: And we're talking about millions of people who lose power because ERCOT's trying to save the energy system.
sentences.zh: 我们说的是数以百万计的人失去了电力，因为ERCOT试图拯救能源系统。

sentences.en: And finally, it works.
sentences.zh: 最终，它奏效了。

sentences.en: The grid begins to stabilize.
sentences.zh: 电网开始稳定下来。

sentences.en: There were only four minutes and 37 seconds before that nine minutes was up.
sentences.zh: 距离那9分钟的期限只剩下4分37秒了。

sentences.en: The grid would have totally failed.
sentences.zh: 否则电网就会彻底崩溃。

sentences.en: And so this is when millions of people start waking up on Monday morning without any power.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么周一早上数以百万计的人醒来时发现没有任何电力。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Including me.
sentences.zh: 包括我。

sentences.en: Just give a sense of how icy things are now.
sentences.zh: 感受一下现在有多冷。

sentences.en: I went to get this cooler in and I realized I have to get this big, thick layer of ice off of it before I can even get back to the house.
sentences.zh: 我去拿这个冷藏箱时，意识到我必须先把它上面那层厚厚的冰敲掉，才能回到屋里。

sentences.en: I tried to document as much as I could at that time.
sentences.zh: 我当时尽可能多地记录下了这一切。

sentences.en: It was like nothing I'd ever lived through before.
sentences.zh: 那是我从未经历过的。

sentences.en: And so, like, what are you feeling at this point?
sentences.zh: 那么，你当时是什么感觉？

sentences.en: Like, it's enough of an anomaly.
sentences.zh: 这已经足够反常了。

sentences.en: You don't are you aren't aware of all the things that are coming.
sentences.zh: 你根本不知道接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: Like, what are you feeling when you wake up and see your breath in the morning in Texas?
sentences.zh: 当你早上在德克萨斯醒来，看到自己呼出的白气时，你是什么感觉？

sentences.en: Like a lot of people, I was nervous.
sentences.zh: 像很多人一样，我很紧张。

sentences.en: The weather was only getting colder.
sentences.zh: 天气只会越来越冷。

sentences.en: And at first, you kind of figure the power is going to come back on quickly because that's the way it's always happened before.
sentences.zh: 起初，你以为电力很快就会恢复，因为以前总是这样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: These are called rolling blackouts.
sentences.zh: 这被称为“轮流停电”。

sentences.en: But but they weren't rolling.
sentences.zh: 但……但它们并没有轮流。

sentences.en: See, typically, if this happens, Texans will see their lights go out for an hour or two and then they'll come back on and the blackout moves to somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 你看，通常情况下，如果发生这种情况，德克萨斯人会经历一两个小时的停电，然后电力恢复，停电会转移到其他地方。

sentences.en: And the idea there is to spread the inconvenience of the power cut around.
sentences.zh: 这样做的目的是为了分摊停电带来的不便。

sentences.en: But again, on Monday, that just isn't happening.
sentences.zh: 但周一那天，这种情况并没有发生。

sentences.en: As far as the temperature in the house, it dropped down like faSt.
sentences.zh: 至于屋里的温度，下降得非常快。

sentences.en: This is Carolyn Rivera.
sentences.zh: 这是卡罗琳·里维拉（Carolyn Rivera）。

sentences.en: She's a retired schoolteacher I spoke with for our series.
sentences.zh: 她是一位退休教师，我为我们的系列节目采访过她。

sentences.en: It was so cold in here.
sentences.zh: 屋里太冷了。

sentences.en: My bed was like a block of ice and it was like I couldn't put on enough clothes to warm myself up.
sentences.zh: 我的床就像一块冰，我穿多少衣服都暖和不过来。

sentences.en: We're going to keep circling back to Carolyn, whose experience in this blackout is just awful.
sentences.zh: 我们将不断回到卡罗琳的故事，她在这次停电中的经历简直太可怕了。

sentences.en: But I do want to take a beat here and just say how dangerous it is for people to lose electricity for extended periods of time.
sentences.zh: 但我确实想在这里停顿一下，说一下人们长时间失去电力是多么危险。

sentences.en: There are people who count on power to run medical equipment, like to get dialysis, for example, and losing power means that they're unable to get these kinds of treatments.
sentences.zh: 有些人依靠电力来运行医疗设备，比如进行透析，失去电力意味着他们无法获得这些治疗。

sentences.en: So, you know, what might just be a discomfort for some people could cost other people their lives,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，对某些人来说可能只是不便的事情，却可能让其他人付出生命的代价，

sentences.en: which makes this whole next chunk of tape I'm going to play you kind of infuriating.
sentences.zh: 这让我接下来要播放的这段录音听起来非常令人愤怒。

sentences.en: As you all know, we are in an unprecedented event throughout last night and all day today.
sentences.zh: 正如大家所知，昨晚和今天一整天，我们都处于一场前所未有的事件中。

sentences.en: This is Deanne Walker.
sentences.zh: 这是迪安·沃克（Deanne Walker）。

sentences.en: She was the chair of the Public Utility Commission.
sentences.zh: 她是公用事业委员会的主席。

sentences.en: The PUC oversees ERCOT, and they met here to talk about the energy market.
sentences.zh: PUC监管着ERCOT，他们在这里开会讨论能源市场。

sentences.en: I believe that there are some current situations within the ERCOT market that are causing what I'll call distortions.
sentences.zh: 我相信ERCOT市场内目前存在一些情况，导致了所谓的“扭曲”。

sentences.en: It may be the wrong term, but that's what I'm going to call it right now.
sentences.zh: 这可能用词不当，但目前我只能这么称呼它。

sentences.en: Distortion seems to be underselling it a bit.
sentences.zh: “扭曲”这个词似乎还不足以形容它。

sentences.en: I'd say super underselling it.
sentences.zh: 我会说这简直是严重低估了。

sentences.en: You know, we've been in loadshed since about one o'clock this morning and that the prices weren't at the scarcity pricing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们从今天凌晨一点左右就开始减负荷了，而价格并没有达到稀缺定价的水平。

sentences.en: And I was somewhat surprised about that, sadly, to say.
sentences.zh: 我很遗憾地说，对此我感到有些惊讶。

sentences.en: So explain this to me.
sentences.zh: 所以给我解释一下。

sentences.en: So what is she talking about here?
sentences.zh: 她在这里到底在说什么？

sentences.en: What Deanne Walker is saying is that she's surprised that the market didn't respond the way it was supposed to.
sentences.zh: 迪安·沃克的意思是，她很惊讶市场没有按照预期做出反应。

sentences.en: You see, state regulators expected that energy prices would go as high as possible.
sentences.zh: 你看，州监管机构预计能源价格会尽可能高。

sentences.en: Higher prices would mean more power plants start generating more power.
sentences.zh: 价格越高，意味着更多的发电厂开始生产更多的电力。

sentences.en: And so did that happen?
sentences.zh: 那么这发生了吗？

sentences.en: Were more power plants generating more power?
sentences.zh: 有更多的发电厂在生产更多的电力吗？

sentences.en: No, because like we said, there were no more power plants left.
sentences.zh: 没有，因为正如我们所说，已经没有更多的发电厂可用了。

sentences.en: Power plants weren't working.
sentences.zh: 发电厂无法运作。

sentences.en: But that didn't stop the Public Utility Commission from meeting and really using the only tool they felt like they had.
sentences.zh: 但这并没有阻止公用事业委员会开会，并动用他们认为自己唯一拥有的工具。

sentences.en: They stepped in and they raised the price of electricity themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们介入并亲自提高了电价。

sentences.en: Because that's the market mechanism that's supposed to bring more power to the grid.
sentences.zh: 因为这就是所谓的市场机制，理应为电网带来更多电力。

sentences.en: But really, the failure here has nothing to do with money.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，这次故障与金钱毫无关系。

sentences.en: Like these are physical plants that are going down.
sentences.zh: 因为这些都是实实在在停摆的发电厂。

sentences.en: So they can throw as much money as they want to.
sentences.zh: 所以他们就算投入再多钱也无济于事。

sentences.en: But it just doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 根本没用。

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: But we created a system where like this was the only lever they felt like they could pull to try to get things back working again.
sentences.zh: 但我们建立了一个系统，让他们觉得这是唯一能用来尝试恢复运作的手段。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was just like this market orthodoxy took over and they ignored the physical reality of the grid.
sentences.zh: 是啊，就像这种市场正统观念占据了主导，而他们却忽视了电网的物理现实。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And as we entered the second day and the third day of this blackout, things just got worse.
sentences.zh: 随着停电进入第二天和第三天，情况变得越来越糟。

sentences.en: Electricity wasn't the only problem.
sentences.zh: 电力并不是唯一的问题。

sentences.en: Natural gas pipelines were breaking down too.
sentences.zh: 天然气管道也出现了故障。

sentences.en: And in Texas during the winter, the main source of fuel that powers the entire grid is natural gas.
sentences.zh: 在德克萨斯的冬天，为整个电网供电的主要燃料来源就是天然气。

sentences.en: So not only is the power that's going out from the power plants, is there a problem there?
sentences.zh: 所以，不仅是发电厂发出的电力出了问题，

sentences.en: But the fuel coming into power plants to make all that energy, that's breaking down too.
sentences.zh: 连输送到发电厂用于生产能源的燃料也供应中断了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then if that wasn't bad enough, the water system starts breaking down.
sentences.zh: 如果这还不够糟糕，供水系统也开始崩溃了。

sentences.en: Water running into people's homes starts to freeze.
sentences.zh: 流向人们家中的水开始结冰。

sentences.en: People's pipes are starting to break all across the state.
sentences.zh: 全州各地的水管开始破裂。

sentences.en: Things just keep compounding and compounding.
sentences.zh: 问题不断叠加，愈演愈烈。

sentences.en: Imagine being in your home without being able to even use the bathroom properly and not having water.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，待在家里连厕所都无法正常使用，而且没有水。

sentences.en: That was horrifying.
sentences.zh: 那太可怕了。

sentences.en: Carolyn's right.
sentences.zh: 卡罗琳说得对。

sentences.en: The whole experience was horrifying.
sentences.zh: 整个经历简直是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: I mean, driving around Austin during the blackout, I saw water shooting out of broken pipes onto the streets and freezing on the streets.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在停电期间开车经过奥斯汀时，我看到水从破裂的管道喷涌到街上，并在街面上结冰。

sentences.en: I went to this one apartment complex.
sentences.zh: 我去过一个公寓大楼。

sentences.en: There was a busted raw sewage pipe on the second floor.
sentences.zh: 二楼有一根破裂的污水管。

sentences.en: So this raw sewage was just spilling out everywhere, like down the stairway into the parking lot.
sentences.zh: 所以未经处理的污水到处溢出，顺着楼梯流进了停车场。

sentences.en: It was really, it was wild.
sentences.zh: 那场面真是太疯狂了。

sentences.en: How did you end up faring for those four or five hectic days?
sentences.zh: 那四五天混乱的日子里，你们是怎么熬过来的？

sentences.en: I mean, when did you get your power back?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你们什么时候恢复供电的？

sentences.en: We were pretty lucky.
sentences.zh: 我们还算幸运。

sentences.en: You know, we lost power on our house for a few days.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们家停电了几天。

sentences.en: But KUT, it's the station where I work.
sentences.zh: 但 KUT，就是我工作的电台。

sentences.en: They put me and my family up at a hotel near the station because I was trying to report on all this too, right?
sentences.zh: 他们把我和家人安置在电台附近的一家酒店，因为我也在试图报道这一切，对吧？

sentences.en: So they put us up after the first night we spent at home in the cold and then we got to move to a hotel.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在家挨了一晚上的冻之后，他们就把我们安置到了酒店。

sentences.en: And that was on what they call a critical circuit.
sentences.zh: 而且那是在他们所谓的“关键电路”上。

sentences.en: There's this kind of huge point of contention, actually, that came up in this crisis.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这次危机中出现了一个巨大的争议点。

sentences.en: And you'd see people post a lot of angry videos online about this too because some parts of every community never lost power.
sentences.zh: 你也会看到人们在网上发布很多愤怒的视频，因为每个社区都有一些地方从未停电。

sentences.en: And that all depended on what kind of a circuit they were on, where they were getting their electricity from.
sentences.zh: 这完全取决于他们所在的电路类型，以及他们从哪里获取电力。

sentences.en: And so you'd see things like, you know, all of the businesses in like downtown Austin, a lot of the high-rise office buildings and stuff,
sentences.zh: 所以你会看到，比如奥斯汀市中心的所有企业，很多高层办公楼之类的，

sentences.en: electricity stayed up and running there the whole time.
sentences.zh: 那里的电力一直保持正常运行。

sentences.en: And you'd see people comment about this also during like the live streams of the public officials like ERCOT and the PUC.
sentences.zh: 在 ERCOT 和 PUC 等政府官员的直播中，你也会看到人们对此发表评论。

sentences.en: People would just become livid.
sentences.zh: 人们简直气疯了。

sentences.en: They'd look at these people sitting comfortably in their well-heated office buildings, sitting there cozy, you know, while millions of other people were just freezing, you know,
sentences.zh: 他们看着这些人舒适地坐在供暖充足的办公楼里，安逸地待着，而与此同时，数以百万计的人却在挨冻，

sentences.en: just trying to figure out what was going to come next.
sentences.zh: 只能试图弄清楚接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: So these critical circuit areas downtown where there's fancy offices and such, they fared better than the places that are less affluent.
sentences.zh: 所以这些市中心有高档办公室之类的关键电路区域，比那些不那么富裕的地方过得好？

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: That was the impression a lot of people got.
sentences.zh: 这是很多人留下的印象。

sentences.en: And I should say there's a lot of research going on right now about how much grids locally in different parts of the state might really be set up like that.
sentences.zh: 我得说，目前有很多研究正在进行，探讨州内不同地区的本地电网是否真的就是这样设置的。

sentences.en: But, you know, the bottom line is people with less means, you know, were the ones who came out of this the worSt.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，经济条件较差的人，确实是这次事件中受损最严重的。

sentences.en: They had less resources to get out of this whole catastrophe, you know, intact.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有的资源更少，无法在整场灾难中全身而退。

sentences.en: You had played us some tape from Carolyn Rivera where the pipes broke in her house.
sentences.zh: 你之前给我们播放了卡罗琳·里维拉的一段录音，她家里的水管破裂了。

sentences.en: And I mean, she sounded like it was extremely stressful, extremely difficult for her.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听起来她压力极大，处境非常艰难。

sentences.en: How did she fare?
sentences.zh: 她后来怎么样了？

sentences.en: How did she end up?
sentences.zh: 她的结局如何？

sentences.en: Yeah, so Carolyn's from a neighborhood in East Houston that's, you know, low income.
sentences.zh: 是这样，卡罗琳来自东休斯顿的一个低收入社区。

sentences.en: It's a place that had already been really devastated by Hurricane Harvey, you know, some years earlier.
sentences.zh: 那个地方几年前就已经被飓风“哈维”摧毁过一次了。

sentences.en: And people, they were still recovering from that hurricane when this blackout hit.
sentences.zh: 当这次停电来袭时，人们还在从那场飓风中恢复。

sentences.en: And, you know, and so Carolyn and a lot of her neighbors, their homes are on the older side.
sentences.zh: 所以，卡罗琳和她的许多邻居，他们的房子都比较老旧。

sentences.en: They might lack proper insulation.
sentences.zh: 可能缺乏适当的隔热层。

sentences.en: And it was in homes like these where the pipes were most likely to burSt.
sentences.zh: 正是在这样的房子里，水管最容易爆裂。

sentences.en: Carolyn said, and she's on a fixed income, I should ask.
sentences.zh: 卡罗琳说，而且我得问一下，她是靠固定收入生活的。

sentences.en: She brings in about $1,500 a month.
sentences.zh: 她每月收入大约 1500 美元。

sentences.en: She said her repairs from the storm totaled more than $3,000.
sentences.zh: 她说风暴造成的维修费用总计超过 3000 美元。

sentences.en: You just don't have that kind of money laying around to pay that type of expense for repair.
sentences.zh: 你根本拿不出那么多钱来支付这种维修费用。

sentences.en: So for a while after the storm, the state didn't allow electric companies to cut people's power.
sentences.zh: 所以风暴过后的一段时间里，政府不允许电力公司切断人们的电源。

sentences.en: There was this moratorium on cutoffs.
sentences.zh: 当时有一个禁止断电的暂停令。

sentences.en: But by the time I talked to Carolyn a few months after the blackout, it had been lifted.
sentences.zh: 但当我停电几个月后采访卡罗琳时，这个禁令已经被取消了。

sentences.en: So people in her situation, people in her community were facing disconnections again.
sentences.zh: 所以像她这样处境的人，她社区里的人，再次面临被断电的风险。

sentences.en: But this time, not because of the blackout, but because of the bills stemming from the blackout.
sentences.zh: 但这次不是因为停电，而是因为停电带来的账单。

sentences.en: So, you know, she was worried she couldn't pay her bill.
sentences.zh: 所以，她很担心自己付不起账单。

sentences.en: And that risk, the risk of being disconnected, was forcing her to start rationing her own electricity.
sentences.zh: 而那种风险，那种被断电的风险，迫使她开始限制自己的用电。

sentences.en: During the day, I turned my air way up to like 83.
sentences.zh: 白天，我把空调开得很高，调到 83 度左右。

sentences.en: And then when I go to bed at night, then I'll drop it down a little lower so I can rest because of the fear of getting an electric bill that I'm not able to pay.
sentences.zh: 晚上睡觉时，我会调低一点，这样才能休息，因为害怕收到付不起的电费账单。

sentences.en: It's like in the winter she froze and now in the summer, you know, she'd bake.
sentences.zh: 就像冬天她被冻坏了，现在夏天，她又得被热坏了。

sentences.en: And I asked her, you know, what she thought about everything, about the blackout, about the disconnections.
sentences.zh: 我问她对这一切有什么看法，关于停电，关于断电。

sentences.en: And this is what she told me.
sentences.zh: 这是她告诉我的。

sentences.en: My thoughts were this.
sentences.zh: 我的想法是这样的。

sentences.en: I was disappointed and hurt, but not surprised.
sentences.zh: 我感到失望和受伤，但并不惊讶。

sentences.en: They have already demonstrated how they feel about poor people.
sentences.zh: 他们已经展示了他们是如何看待穷人的。

sentences.en: You understand what I'm saying?
sentences.zh: 你明白我在说什么吗？

sentences.en: For all the talk about markets and efficiency and profits and risk, the thing that really matters, helping the people that the system failed,
sentences.zh: 尽管谈论了那么多关于市场、效率、利润和风险的话题，但真正重要的事情——帮助那些被系统抛弃的人，

sentences.en: that has yet to really enter the conversation here in Texas.
sentences.zh: 在德克萨斯州，这还没有真正进入讨论范围。

sentences.en: They knew this area wasn't going to get any power if there was a major outage.
sentences.zh: 他们知道如果发生重大停电，这个地区是不会有电的。

sentences.en: They knew that.
sentences.zh: 他们知道这一点。

sentences.en: They knew it.
sentences.zh: 他们知道。

sentences.en: They knew it.
sentences.zh: 他们知道。

sentences.en: They do not care.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不在乎。

sentences.en: When we come back, the blame game and whether the Texas grid can survive another major storm.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将讨论“指责游戏”，以及德州电网能否在下一次大风暴中幸存。

sentences.en: So I'm back with Moe's Buchel, who reported all about last year's blackout in Texas.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回来，我与莫·布切尔在一起，他报道了去年德州停电的所有情况。

sentences.en: And you just told us the whole story.
sentences.zh: 你刚刚给我们讲述了整个故事。

sentences.en: But I have a bunch of questions for you.
sentences.zh: 但我还有一堆问题要问你。

sentences.en: And I guess the first and foremost is like, you know, how are things now?
sentences.zh: 我想第一个也是最重要的问题是，现在情况如何？

sentences.en: I know a few weeks back there was another scare with the Texas grid.
sentences.zh: 我知道几周前德州电网又出现了一次恐慌。

sentences.en: How are people feeling these days?
sentences.zh: 这些天人们感觉如何？

sentences.en: I mean, people are still really freaked out, honestly.
sentences.zh: 老实说，人们仍然非常害怕。

sentences.en: Like you mentioned, this whole past winter, we've kind of fallen into this pattern where whenever a cold front comes through,
sentences.zh: 就像你提到的，整个过去这个冬天，我们陷入了一种模式，每当冷锋过境，

sentences.en: it's almost like people are reliving the trauma of what happened last year.
sentences.zh: 人们几乎就像在重温去年发生的创伤。

sentences.en: You see people going to grocery stores and really kind of clearing out the shelves sometimes, preparing for another possible blackout.
sentences.zh: 你会看到人们去杂货店，有时真的会把货架清空，为下一次可能的停电做准备。

sentences.en: There's also just not a lot of confidence, you know, that enough has been done to fix this thing.
sentences.zh: 人们也没有太多的信心，认为已经采取了足够的措施来解决这个问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, we really didn't get into this in the main part of our story, the question of accountability.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们在故事的主体部分并没有深入探讨问责制的问题。

sentences.en: Has anyone been held responsible for the grid failure?
sentences.zh: 有人为电网故障负责了吗？

sentences.en: I noticed, like, when you were announcing different people when they were speaking, you used the word former a lot, the former head of things.
sentences.zh: 我注意到，当你介绍不同的人发言时，你经常使用“前任”这个词，比如“前任负责人”。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: So, like, is that part of the accountability?
sentences.zh: 所以，这是问责制的一部分吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: Up to a certain level, everybody in charge of the electric system of Texas was gone within a few weeks of this happening.
sentences.zh: 在一定程度上，德州电力系统的所有负责人在这件事发生后的几周内都离职了。

sentences.en: All the public utility commissioners and also Bill Magnus, he was the head of ERCOT.
sentences.zh: 所有的公用事业委员，还有比尔·马格努斯，他是 ERCOT 的负责人。

sentences.en: But I think it's safe to say that ERCOT was initially sort of the focus of that anger.
sentences.zh: 但我认为可以肯定地说，ERCOT 最初是那种愤怒的焦点。

sentences.en: I totally get that people could be or even should be mad at ERCOT.
sentences.zh: 我完全理解人们可能会，甚至应该对 ERCOT 感到愤怒。

sentences.en: But how much could they realistically do?
sentences.zh: 但他们实际上能做多少呢？

sentences.en: Because, like, their hands were sort of tied by this system that this group of politicians created back in the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 因为他们的手脚被这群政客在 90 年代建立的系统束缚住了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, especially when it came to ERCOT, like, there were other people that would come forward and say, like, these are just kind of the technocrats.
sentences.zh: 是的，尤其是提到 ERCOT 时，会有其他人站出来说，这些人只是技术官僚。

sentences.en: You know, these are the people that are running the machine that someone else built.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些人只是在操作别人建造的机器。

sentences.en: In fact, Bill Magnus, the former head of ERCOT, said exactly as much when justifying their decision to cut power the first night of the blackout.
sentences.zh: 事实上，ERCOT 前负责人比尔·马格努斯在为停电第一晚切断电源的决定辩护时，正是这么说的。

sentences.en: The fundamental decision that was made to have the outages imposed was a wise decision by the operators that we have here.
sentences.zh: 实施停电的根本决定，是我们这里的操作员做出的明智决定。

sentences.en: If we had waited, not done outages, not reduced demand, Texas would be in an indeterminately long situation without power even more extensively than we are with these outages.
sentences.zh: 如果我们等待，不进行停电，不减少需求，德州将陷入更长时间的停电状态，其影响范围甚至比我们现在实施停电的情况还要广泛。

sentences.en: So there is the former, you know, ERCOT CEO basically saying, we did our job, you know, that the grid didn't fully melt down.
sentences.zh: 所以，那位前 ERCOT 首席执行官基本上是在说：我们完成了我们的工作，电网没有完全崩溃。

sentences.en: So for us, like, that's a win.
sentences.zh: 所以对我们来说，这算是一场胜利。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: They succeeded in fulfilling their mandate.
sentences.zh: 他们成功完成了他们的使命。

sentences.en: And that's basically it.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是这样。

sentences.en: Right, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，是的。

sentences.en: And in doing that, you know, millions of people, well, you know what happened.
sentences.zh: 而在这样做的时候，你知道，数百万人，好吧，你知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So as ERCOT is passing the buck, who does it land to next?
sentences.zh: 那么，当 ERCOT 推卸责任时，下一个该轮到谁了？

sentences.en: So this really was, it was like this string of finger pointing going on in Austin for months after this thing happened.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一场持续数月的指责游戏，在奥斯汀上演了很久。

sentences.en: So first you had the power generators, another obvious party that's responsible for this.
sentences.zh: 首先是发电商，这是另一个显然要对此负责的群体。

sentences.en: These are the companies that own the power plants that failed to produce the electricity.
sentences.zh: 这些公司拥有未能发电的发电厂。

sentences.en: And so there's a lot of focus on them.
sentences.zh: 所以人们把很多注意力集中在他们身上。

sentences.en: What are you guys going to do to make sure this never happens again?
sentences.zh: 你们打算做什么来确保这种情况永远不会再发生？

sentences.en: But almost right out of the gate, the first thing you heard from the power plants was that it's not all our fault because we didn't have the fuel to run.
sentences.zh: 但几乎从一开始，发电厂说的第一件事就是：这不全是我们的错，因为我们没有燃料来运行。

sentences.en: Like the power generators are literally saying, and this is backed up by data, it's not just them saying this.
sentences.zh: 就像发电商们确实在说，而且有数据支持，不仅仅是他们这么说，

sentences.en: The natural gas supply dropped so hard, so fast that they could not run their plants to produce electricity.
sentences.zh: 天然气供应下降得太厉害、太快了，以至于他们无法运行电厂来发电。

sentences.en: So their argument then is like, we could be as ready for a storm as ever, but if we don't have fuel to run, it's never going to help anything.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的论点是，我们可以像往常一样为风暴做好准备，但如果没有燃料运行，什么都帮不上忙。

sentences.en: So they point their fingers to the natural gas suppliers.
sentences.zh: 于是他们把矛头指向了天然气供应商。

sentences.en: And so after that, like, does the natural gas company, you know, like flame somebody else?
sentences.zh: 那么在那之后，天然气公司会指责别人吗？

sentences.en: They absolutely did.
sentences.zh: 他们绝对指责了。

sentences.en: I mean, the line from the natural gas industry was that their power had been cut by ERCOT.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，天然气行业的说法是，他们的电力被 ERCOT 切断了。

sentences.en: And so they couldn't produce natural gas to bring to the power generators because they were victims of the blackout, essentially.
sentences.zh: 所以他们无法生产天然气来供应给发电商，因为他们本质上也是停电的受害者。

sentences.en: That was their line.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们的说辞。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So, I mean, was there any truth to that?
sentences.zh: 所以，这里面有什么真相吗？

sentences.en: That sounds horrifying.
sentences.zh: 听起来太可怕了。

sentences.en: That's like a circular firing squad.
sentences.zh: 这简直就是一场循环的互相残杀。

sentences.en: That's horrible.
sentences.zh: 那太可怕了。

sentences.en: Yeah, there is truth to it, but it's not the whole story.
sentences.zh: 没错，这确实有一定道理，但并非事情的全貌。

sentences.en: The problem with that kind of rationalization is that a lot of the natural gas supply dropped not because of power cuts.
sentences.zh: 这种合理化解释的问题在于，很多天然气供应中断并非是因为停电。

sentences.en: And, in fact, a lot of the natural gas supply in the state of Texas started dropping well before the blackouts were enacting.
sentences.zh: 事实上，德克萨斯州的许多天然气供应在停电发生前就已经开始大幅下降了。

sentences.en: We saw natural gas supply get really scarce even in the lead up to this storm.
sentences.zh: 我们看到，甚至在暴风雪来临之前，天然气供应就已经非常紧缺了。

sentences.en: So it can't all be blamed on ERCOT.
sentences.zh: 所以这不能全怪德州电力可靠性委员会（ERCOT）。

sentences.en: I mean, and one of the aspects of accountability is, like, who's going to pay for it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，问责制的一个方面是，谁来为此买单？

sentences.en: Because you mentioned that the Texas Public Utility Commission raised the price of electricity to its maximum.
sentences.zh: 因为你提到德州公用事业委员会将电价提高到了最高限额。

sentences.en: That was like $9,000 per megawatt hour.
sentences.zh: 那可是每兆瓦时9000美元。

sentences.en: And then, as I understand it, the people are on the hook for that, right?
sentences.zh: 据我理解，这笔费用最终是由民众承担的，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, like, there's a lot of reporting around this after the blackout.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，停电之后有很多关于此事的报道。

sentences.en: And initially, what you might have heard a lot about are these, like, super high electric bills, thousands of dollars of bills.
sentences.zh: 起初，你可能听到了很多关于这些超高额电费的消息，账单高达数千美元。

sentences.en: And that did affect some people in the state who had certain plans, you know, electric plans.
sentences.zh: 这确实影响了州内一些选择了特定电力计划的居民。

sentences.en: But the reality is, for most Texans, everyone's bill is going to be a little higher for decades to come.
sentences.zh: 但现实情况是，对于大多数德州人来说，未来几十年的电费都会稍微高一些。

sentences.en: This blackout created this kind of massive wealth transfer, essentially.
sentences.zh: 这次停电本质上造成了一种大规模的财富转移。

sentences.en: And all of this debt got transferred from power companies that had to pay these huge prices for electricity and also for natural gas.
sentences.zh: 所有的债务都从那些不得不支付高昂电价和天然气价格的电力公司转移出去了。

sentences.en: All of that debt is filtering back to the ratepayer now.
sentences.zh: 现在，所有这些债务都转嫁到了纳税人身上。

sentences.en: And it's going to be paid off in small increments month by month over decades.
sentences.zh: 而且这些债务将在未来几十年里，以每月小额分期的方式偿还。

sentences.en: And we're talking, again, billions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 我们再次强调，这涉及数十亿美元。

sentences.en: So this is also still a very live issue.
sentences.zh: 所以这仍然是一个非常现实的问题。

sentences.en: People are really pissed off about this.
sentences.zh: 人们对此感到非常愤怒。

sentences.en: And they feel like they were victimized by this blackout, and now they've got to foot the bill and pay billions to these companies that benefited from this energy scarcity.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得自己在这次停电中成了受害者，现在却不得不买单，向那些从能源短缺中获利的公司支付数十亿美元。

sentences.en: So, like, in the end, if you were to balance all the scales, you know, like,
sentences.zh: 所以，最终，如果你要权衡利弊，你知道，

sentences.en: the argument for deregulation was that it was supposed to make the whole system cheaper and efficient and that those savings would be felt by the consumer.
sentences.zh: 当初支持放松管制的理由是，它应该使整个系统更便宜、更高效，消费者能从中受益。

sentences.en: That's what they always say.
sentences.zh: 他们总是这么说。

sentences.en: But this doesn't sound cheaper.
sentences.zh: 但这听起来并不便宜。

sentences.en: No, I've seen a lot of studies on this.
sentences.zh: 不，我看了很多关于这方面的研究。

sentences.en: And there are, of course, a lot of competing studies.
sentences.zh: 当然，也有很多相互矛盾的研究。

sentences.en: But most of what I've seen shows that, on average, your regular ratepayer, your residential consumer, did not see cheaper electricity after deregulation.
sentences.zh: 但我看到的大多数研究表明，平均而言，普通纳税人，即住宅用户，在放松管制后并没有享受到更便宜的电力。

sentences.en: There are some people who say that the bigger customers, the industrial customers, they got cheaper power.
sentences.zh: 有些人说，那些大客户，即工业客户，确实获得了更便宜的电力。

sentences.en: But your average person at home didn't necessarily see better prices.
sentences.zh: 但普通家庭用户并没有享受到更好的价格。

sentences.en: And then if you add on to the fact of the billions of dollars people will now be paying off because of the blackout, well, that certainly, again,
sentences.zh: 再加上人们现在因为停电而要偿还数十亿美元的事实，嗯，这当然再次意味着，

sentences.en: means that our system in Texas is even more expensive now, you know, than it was before the blackout.
sentences.zh: 我们在德州的系统现在比停电前更贵了。

sentences.en: But so, yeah, in terms of price, it's hard to make an argument for the system that they created when they deregulated.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，就价格而言，很难为他们放松管制后所建立的系统辩护。

sentences.en: So beyond, you know, figuring out who to blame, have there been any reforms that have been put in place last February so that something like this doesn't happen again?
sentences.zh: 那么，除了追究责任之外，去年二月以来是否采取了任何改革措施，以防止类似事件再次发生？

sentences.en: Yeah, there were.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实有。

sentences.en: Again, you know, lawmakers met.
sentences.zh: 同样，立法者们开了会。

sentences.en: They passed some laws.
sentences.zh: 他们通过了一些法律。

sentences.en: Because one thing that they did was they said power plants have to winterize.
sentences.zh: 他们做的一件事是要求发电厂必须进行防寒改造。

sentences.en: Basically, you've got to insulate yourself so you can run in the cold weather.
sentences.zh: 基本上，你必须做好隔热措施，这样才能在寒冷天气下运行。

sentences.en: Power plants did do that last fall, before this winter.
sentences.zh: 发电厂在去年秋天，即这个冬天之前，确实做了这些工作。

sentences.en: Parts of the natural gas system also are now not supposed to have their power cut in a blackout, which sounds like it could be helpful.
sentences.zh: 天然气系统的部分设施现在也不允许在停电时被切断电源，这听起来似乎会有所帮助。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: But the natural gas infrastructure has not winterized.
sentences.zh: 但天然气基础设施并没有进行防寒改造。

sentences.en: And, you know, regulators are still working on that.
sentences.zh: 监管机构仍在为此努力。

sentences.en: It's something that they hope to have done next winter.
sentences.zh: 他们希望在明年冬天之前完成这项工作。

sentences.en: But that process has been a lot slower and a lot more controversial, honestly, the fact that the natural gas companies have not had to do that yet.
sentences.zh: 但老实说，这个过程非常缓慢且充满争议，因为天然气公司至今还不需要这样做。

sentences.en: Is there any notion of just getting like a real significant line out to other electrical grids in the United States, you know, just like emergencies or something?
sentences.zh: 有没有考虑过建立一条通往美国其他电网的真正重要的线路，你知道，以备紧急情况之需？

sentences.en: That has been a big topic of conversation.
sentences.zh: 这已经成为一个重要的讨论话题。

sentences.en: And, you know, we've heard a lot of people come out and say that not only should we do that,
sentences.zh: 我们听到很多人出来说，我们不仅应该这样做，

sentences.en: but that many of them argue that we can do it in Texas without even giving up our independent control of the grid, right?
sentences.zh: 而且许多人认为，我们可以在不放弃对电网独立控制权的情况下在德州实现这一点，对吧？

sentences.en: We wouldn't necessarily have to have to have tons of federal oversight.
sentences.zh: 我们不一定非要有大量的联邦监管。

sentences.en: So, you know, that's a conversation that's going on.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个正在进行的对话。

sentences.en: But it's not really clear whether our state leadership wants to go in that direction.
sentences.zh: 但目前还不清楚我们的州领导层是否想朝这个方向发展。

sentences.en: I think there's still this idea that this was a historic freeze, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为人们仍然认为这是一次历史性的冰冻灾害，对吧？

sentences.en: This is something that Texas hardly ever sees happen.
sentences.zh: 这是德州几乎从未发生过的事情。

sentences.en: So maybe people are wondering why make an investment to fix a system that really works most of the time.
sentences.zh: 所以也许人们在想，为什么要投资去修复一个在大多数时候都能正常工作的系统呢？

sentences.en: I mean, I guess people can comfort themselves with the idea that the system worked most of the time.
sentences.zh: 我想人们可以用“系统在大多数时候都能正常工作”这种想法来安慰自己。

sentences.en: But, you know, we're talking about people's electricity.
sentences.zh: 但是，我们谈论的是人们的电力供应。

sentences.en: Shouldn't that work all the time?
sentences.zh: 难道不应该一直正常工作吗？

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And another problem with the idea that the system works most of the time is that these storms are happening more often because of climate change.
sentences.zh: 而且“系统在大多数时候都能正常工作”这一想法的另一个问题是，由于气候变化，这些风暴发生的频率越来越高。

sentences.en: And here I'm not just talking about cold spells, right?
sentences.zh: 我指的不仅仅是寒流，对吧？

sentences.en: We have things like hurricanes.
sentences.zh: 我们还有飓风之类的灾害。

sentences.en: I mean, Hurricane Harvey really wrecked Houston and a big part of the state not so long ago.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不久前飓风“哈维”确实摧毁了休斯顿和该州的大部分地区。

sentences.en: We have massive droughts.
sentences.zh: 我们还有大规模的干旱。

sentences.en: You know, we can get months and months at a time of triple-digit heat.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们可能会连续几个月经历三位数的高温。

sentences.en: That also has its own effect on the grid.
sentences.zh: 这对电网也有其自身的影响。

sentences.en: And so it's becoming less and less possible to just say, oh, you know, this is going to happen every few decades.
sentences.zh: 所以，仅仅说“哦，这几十年才会发生一次”已经越来越不可能了。

sentences.en: And we don't really need a plan around it because that's just not the case anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要围绕它制定计划，因为情况已经不再是那样了。

sentences.en: Well, Moe's, I really appreciate you sharing your story with us and telling it to our audience.
sentences.zh: 好吧，Moe's，非常感谢你与我们分享你的故事，并告诉我们的听众。

sentences.en: And I highly recommend people go listen to The Disconnect.
sentences.zh: 我强烈推荐大家去听听《The Disconnect》。

sentences.en: It's fascinating, this section of the whole event, and really worth checking out no matter where you're from.
sentences.zh: 整个事件的这一部分非常引人入胜，无论你来自哪里，都非常值得一听。

sentences.en: I really appreciate it, Roman.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，Roman。

sentences.zh: 非常感谢。
